risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Nearly 60% of new hotels outside major cities report staffing shortages, particularly in F&B, front office and engineering roles, an industry-wide pressure the company operates within.
- Geopolitical tensions involving the United States, Israel and Iran are disrupting global energy markets and aviation networks, raising airfares and travel uncertainty, which could affect hotels, travel companies and consumer travel behaviour.
- Last-mile connectivity remains inconsistent especially in pilgrimage towns, hill stations and heritage zones, and approval processes for hotel projects continue to be slow and inconsistent across states, with elevated borrowing costs.
- Climate volatility and crowd surges during festivals and pilgrimage seasons strain infrastructure and guest experience.
- Over-dependence on online travel agencies continues to compress margins and weaken brand control across the industry.
- Hospitality businesses are preparing for increased operating costs linked to fuel inflation and supply-chain disruptions, facing higher expenses for transportation, imported products, logistics and food procurement if global instability continues.
- The Board's risk management disclosure lists regulation, competition, business risk (financial, political, legal), technology obsolescence, investments, retention of talent, and expansion of facilities as the common risks the company manages via its Risk Management Policy.
- Certain related-party transactions from earlier years are part of a legal case pending before the NCLT, New Delhi; the Board has deferred approving them pending the NCLT's decision, and they remain outside the Section 189 register.
